notes: §1985:IV.6.3.2.2 says the format "defines the order of their presentation in the source program", and §1985:IV.6.3.2.2.1 prints DATA DIVISION., then five optional sections in the order FILE, WORKING-STORAGE, LINKAGE, COMMUNICATION, REPORT, with "file-description-entry {record-description-entry} ...". The PARTIAL arm (an FD with a RECORD clause and no record description entry compiled at 85 through MaterializeImpliedRecord, the 2002 permission) is fixed by kb/Work PB5071: below 2002 the FD is refused COBOL1837 citing §1985:VII.3.2.3 SR3 (VIII and IX for relative and indexed files); a report file stays exempt. Every other arm was probed right at --std 85 by the 1985 code read (2026-11-10): sections in order and once each, the 2002 additions refused (COBOL0900), the SD and RD requirements (COBOL1837, COBOL2708), a record after a report FD (COBOL2578), level 77 under an FD or CD (COBOL1746).

next.reason: 1985 data division: FILE SECTION (file-description-entry {record-description-entry} …, sort-merge entries, report-file-description-entry), WORKING-STORAGE, LINKAGE, COMMUNICATION and REPORT sections. §2023:13.2.1 (with the section formats §2023:13.4.2, §2023:13.5.2, §2023:13.7.2 and §2023:13.8.2 restating it) has no COMMUNICATION SECTION, so a 1985 program with one is refused; it lets a file-description-entry have no record-description-entry ([ … ] …), adds constant-entry and type-declaration-entry, and adds LOCAL-STORAGE and SCREEN sections.
